newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 3.172 billion stg in August.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 3.172 billion stg in August.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the UK private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 3.172 billion stg in August, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said.
This was up from July's 2.749 billion stg increase but slightly below the six-monthly average of 3.4 billion.
Consumer credit rose by 453 million stg, down from 556 million in July and compared with a recent monthly average of 405 million.
Mortgage lending was up 632 million stg after a July rise of 612 million and above the recent monthly average of 621 million.
BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said the trend in lending remained strong.

"Consumer credit, though not matching the buoyant July figure, recorded another strong increase, whilst mortgage lending, now including the former National & Provincial building society, was close to the recent monthly average," he said.
Within the consumer credit bracket, credit card credit rose by 210 million stg in August.
Lending to the financial sector rose by 603 million stg. down from a 1.099 billion stg increase in July.
"Following a repayment in the previous month, there was a return to borrowing by industrial and commercial companies in August," Sweeney said.
